parsed_output.refined_idea: For individuals cooking for one or two people, provide personalized meal suggestions based on manually entered pantry items and their approximate expiration dates, then test whether this reduces food waste and changes cooking behavior.
parsed_output.core_mechanism: Manual entry of pantry items with approximate expiration dates to generate personalized meal suggestions for individuals cooking for one or two people.
parsed_output.core_mechanism_justification: Directly reflects the user's explicit intent to evaluate the impact of such suggestions on behavior and waste, avoiding reliance on automated data capture methods.

accepted_changes.proposal: Add gamification and social rewards to encourage ingredient registration and suggestion acceptance
accepted_changes.promotion_reason: Enhances user engagement and data accuracy, supporting the core hypothesis
accepted_changes.evidence_or_decision_basis: User studies show gamification improves adherence to self‑reporting tasks

candidate_possibilities: Introduce voice input for pantry entry to simplify manual data collection

rejected_changes.proposal: Implement barcode scanning and image recognition for automatic ingredient capture
rejected_changes.reason_rejected: Requires camera access, complex ML models, and raises privacy/battery concerns; not essential for core validation

rejected_changes.proposal: Connect to smart appliances and waste sensors for automatic tracking
rejected_changes.reason_rejected: High hardware cost and limited user base; beyond scope of initial pilot

remaining_uncertainties: Reliability of user‑reported ingredient quantities and expiration dates
Accuracy of measured reduction in food waste
Sustained user adherence to suggested meals over time
known_risks: Privacy concerns over personal food inventory data
Low adoption if suggestions are not appealing or convenient
Potential bias in the suggestion algorithm affecting meal variety
parsed_output.recommended_next_step: Run a pilot study where participants manually log pantry items and expiration dates, receive daily meal suggestions, and track food waste and cooking behavior over a 4‑week period, while monitoring engagement and gathering feedback on the gamification features.
